pack.title: Unexpected Connections
pack.description: Eight fresh puzzles revealing surprising links across language, culture, science, and everyday life.

categories.title: HEADWEAR
categories.triviaFact: The sombrero takes its name from the Spanish word sombra, meaning shade, which its wide brim provides.

categories.title: BIRDS OF PREY
categories.triviaFact: The osprey feeds almost entirely on live fish, plunging feet first into the water to catch them.

categories.title: GOLF SCORING TERMS
categories.triviaFact: In golf, a birdie is one stroke under par for a hole, while an eagle is two strokes under.

categories.title: PARTS OF A CAR
categories.triviaFact: Bonnet and boot are the British names for what American drivers call the hood and trunk of a car.

redHerrings.note: EAGLE looks like a fifth bird of prey beside FALCON, OSPREY, KESTREL and HARRIER, but golf needs it; PAR, BOGEY, BIRDIE and EAGLE are all scoring terms.
BONNET and HOOD are worn on the head like BERET and BEANIE, but they are also car parts; BOOT and TRUNK confirm that reading.

categories.title: ANIMAL ENCLOSURES
categories.triviaFact: A traditional rabbit hutch is often a raised wooden box with a wire mesh front that lets fresh air circulate.

categories.title: WORDS FOR A STRONG DESIRE
categories.triviaFact: Crave comes from an Old English verb meaning to demand, long before it meant to long for something.

categories.title: THINGS WITH A BRIDGE
categories.triviaFact: A ship's bridge is named after the raised walkway that once spanned the paddle wheels of early steamships.

categories.title: CURRENCIES
categories.triviaFact: The yen, the won and the Chinese yuan all take their names from a character meaning round.

redHerrings.note: POUND is a place where stray animals are held, tempting the KENNEL and HUTCH group, but REAL, WON and YEN need it as a currency.
YEN can mean a longing, just like URGE and ITCH, but the desire words are complete without it; it joins REAL, WON and POUND.

categories.title: PUNCTUATION MARKS
categories.triviaFact: Apostrophe comes from a Greek word for turning away, describing a mark that shows where letters were left out.

categories.title: ZODIAC SIGNS
categories.triviaFact: Libra, represented by a pair of scales, is the only zodiac sign symbolized by an object.

categories.title: OLYMPIAN DEITIES
categories.triviaFact: In many versions of the myth, Hephaestus split open the head of Zeus with an axe, and Athena sprang out.

categories.title: NASA HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT PROGRAMS
categories.triviaFact: NASA named its return-to-the-Moon program after Artemis, the twin sister of Apollo in Greek myth.

redHerrings.note: GEMINI looks like a fifth zodiac sign beside ARIES and LIBRA, but it also named the NASA program flown between MERCURY and APOLLO.
APOLLO and ARTEMIS are Olympian twins, suggesting a six-deity set, but ZEUS, APHRODITE, DIONYSUS and HEPHAESTUS complete it; the twins name NASA programs.
MERCURY is also a Roman god and a planet, but it is not one of the Greek Olympians; it opens the list of NASA human spaceflight programs.
ARIES resembles ARES, the Greek god of war, but it is the zodiac ram and belongs with LIBRA, VIRGO and PISCES.

categories.title: US STATES
categories.triviaFact: Vermont's name is usually traced to the French words for green mountain.

categories.title: GARMENTS NAMED AFTER PLACES
categories.triviaFact: Jodhpurs take their name from the Indian city of Jodhpur, where similar riding trousers were worn.

categories.title: COMPUTER FONTS
categories.triviaFact: Helvetica takes its name from Helvetia, the Latin name for Switzerland, where the typeface was created.

categories.title: CARRY LOADS FOR OTHERS
categories.triviaFact: A mule is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse, valued for its strength and stamina.

redHerrings.note: GEORGIA looks like a fifth US state beside OREGON and KANSAS, but it is also a familiar computer font alongside COURIER, IMPACT and HELVETICA.
COURIER carries loads for others like a PORTER or CADDIE, but the font set needs it; MULE completes the carriers.
MULE is also a backless shoe, tempting the garment set, but it is not named after a place; it is the pack animal among the carriers.

categories.title: RODENTS
categories.triviaFact: A rodent's front teeth never stop growing, so regular gnawing keeps them at a useful length.

categories.title: WAYS TO READ
categories.triviaFact: Skimming means reading quickly for the gist, while scanning means searching a text for particular details.

categories.title: SOUTH AMERICAN ANIMALS
categories.triviaFact: Caimans belong to the same family as alligators and live in rivers and wetlands across Central and South America.

categories.title: CONTAIN A HIDDEN COUNTRY
categories.triviaFact: Modern Mali is named after the medieval Mali Empire, which grew wealthy through its trade in gold.

redHerrings.note: CAPYBARA and PIRANHA both live in South America, suggesting a six-animal set, but CAPYBARA is one of the four rodents, the only mammals on the board, and PIRANHA hides IRAN.
PERUSE looks like a fifth way to read beside SKIM and SCAN, but that group is complete with BROWSE and STUDY; PERUSE hides PERU.

categories.title: THINGS THAT FLOAT
categories.triviaFact: Roughly nine tenths of an iceberg's volume lies hidden below the surface of the water.

categories.title: TEN-PIN BOWLING TERMS
categories.triviaFact: In ten-pin bowling, three strikes in a row are called a turkey.

categories.title: BEGIN WITH A BODY PART
categories.triviaFact: Legend comes from a Latin word meaning things to be read, first used for stories of saints' lives.

categories.title: ALSO EUROPEAN CITIES
categories.triviaFact: Much of the old town of Split lies within the walls of a palace that the Roman emperor Diocletian built around 300 AD.

redHerrings.note: CORK floats as surely as BUOY, RAFT and ICEBERG, but it is also a city in Ireland, joining NICE, SPLIT and BATH.
SPLIT is a real bowling term beside STRIKE and SPARE, yet that group is complete with TURKEY and FRAME; SPLIT is a Croatian city.
TURKEY sounds like a place to join the cities, but it is a country rather than a city; in bowling it means three strikes in a row.
An ARMADA floats too, but the floating set is already complete; its opening ARM joins LEGEND, SHINGLE and EARNEST.

categories.title: WORDS FOR GREAT HAPPINESS
categories.triviaFact: Rapture comes from a Latin word for seizing or carrying off, like being swept away by joy.

categories.title: CONIFERS
categories.triviaFact: The larch is an unusual conifer that turns gold and sheds all of its needles every autumn.

categories.title: BEFORE BERRY
categories.triviaFact: Botanically, strawberries and raspberries are not true berries, unlike tomatoes and bananas.

categories.title: CONTAIN ALL FIVE VOWELS
categories.triviaFact: Sequoia fits all five vowels into seven letters, while facetious has them in alphabetical order.

redHerrings.note: SEQUOIA really is a fifth conifer, but the vowel group needs it; SPRUCE, FIR, LARCH and CYPRESS complete the conifers.
ELDER is a flowering broadleaf tree, not a conifer, so it only suits a looser trees theme; it belongs with GOOSE, STRAW and RASP as ELDERBERRY.
EUPHORIA means great happiness like BLISS and RAPTURE, but it belongs with SEQUOIA and EQUATION as a word containing all five vowels.
ELATION almost contains every vowel, but it has no U, so it stays with BLISS, RAPTURE and GLEE.

categories.title: HOUSEHOLD CHORES
categories.triviaFact: One of the first powered vacuum cleaners was so big that a horse had to haul it from job to job.

categories.title: PARTS OF A SMARTPHONE
categories.triviaFact: Many smartphones have several microphones, using the extra ones to help cancel out background noise.

categories.title: DIPLOMACY TERMS
categories.triviaFact: Embargo comes from a Spanish verb meaning to bar, and first meant an order stopping ships from leaving port.

categories.title: CAN MEAN ITS OWN OPPOSITE
categories.triviaFact: Words like these are called contronyms, and cleave can mean both to split apart and to cling together.

redHerrings.note: DUST sounds like a fifth chore beside SWEEP and MOP, but it can mean adding a fine powder as well as removing dirt.
SCREEN is an obvious smartphone part, yet BATTERY, CAMERA, SPEAKER and MICROPHONE already complete that group; it can mean both to show and to hide.
SANCTION sits naturally beside TREATY and EMBARGO, but it can mean both to approve and to punish, so it joins the opposite-meaning words.
